name: C2PA Content Credentials Verification
description: Cryptographically validates C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) manifest data. This standard establishes a verifiable chain of custody by embedding hard-coded provenance and edit histories, definitively proving whether media originated from a compliant camera sensor or an AI generator.
algorithm: C2PA Cryptographic Manifest Parsing and Signature Validation
mechanism: The method extracts JUMBF (JPEG Universal Metadata Box Format) containers from the image binary, isolating the cryptographic CBOR payloads. It validates the X.509 certificate chain to ensure the credentials haven't been tampered with. It strictly checks for AI assertion tags (e.g., `c2pa.created`, `ai_generated`, `trainedAlgorithmicMedia`). If a valid signature matching an AI platform (like OpenAI, Midjourney, or Adobe Firefly) or a camera manufacturer (like Leica or Sony) is found, origin is cryptographically guaranteed.
parameters: Transport: JUMBF superboxes, Payload Format: CBOR, Cryptography: X.509 Certificate Validation, Markers: `c2pa.created`, `ai_generated`
accuracy: Very High (95-100%) - Provides absolute certainty when cryptographic manifests are present and valid, but currently bounded by low global adoption.
useCase: Establishing absolute ground truth for media provenance, verifying true camera origins in journalism, and definitively identifying transparently declared AI generations.

references.title: C2PA Technical Specification 2.0 — Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
Rosenthol, L. et al. (2023). Content Provenance and Authenticity: The C2PA Standard. IEEE Security & Privacy.

strengths:
• Relies on cryptographic digital signatures that are nearly impossible to spoof.
• Provides a complete, transparent edit history directly from the moment of capture.
• Supported by massive industry titans (Adobe, Microsoft, Google, Intel, Sony).
• Offers absolute algorithmic certainty rather than statistical probability.
limitations:
• Manifests are frequently stripped during aggressive social media re-encoding.
• Requires native hardware (C2PA-aware cameras) or specialized software capable of singing.
• Useless against malicious screenshotting or physical analog recapture.
• Still facing extremely low global adoption rates among general smartphone users.
